root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking possession of something by gathering, receiving, or grasping it.
root_idea.development: From physical taking and collecting, the lexical branches extend to receiving, retaining, overpowering, seizing, punishing, adopting or appointing, and the nouns denoting what is taken or a place of taking.

senses.definition: To take, receive, obtain, hold, or take away something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for ordinary taking or receiving, including taking something by hand, receiving something from someone, and taking or removing an object.

senses.definition: To accept, admit, or willingly receive something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for accepting a covenant, obligation, counsel, or something offered for acceptance; the object may be expressed directly or in a related construction.

senses.definition: To retain or detain someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used when a person or object is kept in place, including retaining someone in another's stead.

senses.definition: To seize, overpower, or affect someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: The subject may be a person, an event, a disease, a physical sensation, or another force; the result may be physical seizure, overpowering influence, or being affected by it.
Used of taking a person as a captive or prisoner.

senses.definition: To gain mastery over and kill or slay someone.
senses.usage_conditions: A forceful taking may culminate in overcoming and killing the person taken.

senses.definition: To destroy, exterminate, or bring ruin upon someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of destructive divine or other overwhelming action, especially destruction as a consequence of wrongdoing.

senses.definition: To punish, chastise, or requite someone for an offense.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a person and a sin or offense, often in the construction of taking someone for or because of the wrongdoing.

senses.definition: To hold someone accountable, call someone to account, blame, or punish.
senses.usage_conditions: This Form III usage presents taking as reciprocal or directed accountability for an act, omission, or offense; it may be translated as taking someone to task or calling someone to account.

senses.definition: To take or acquire something for oneself; to adopt, choose, or assume it.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for deliberately selecting, adopting, acquiring, or taking something as one's own, including a course, object, person, or affiliation.

senses.definition: To make, constitute, appoint, or take someone or something as a specified role or status.
senses.usage_conditions: Often transitive to two objects: the first is made or taken as the second, such as a friend, child, ally, object of worship, or subject of derision.

senses.definition: To do or establish a benefit or favor for someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in a construction describing a favor or good deed done for another, sometimes with the implication that the favor becomes an acknowledged benefit.

senses.definition: Taking or receiving; the act of taking.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of أَخَذَ, used for ordinary taking and receiving.
Used for an overwhelming or retributive seizure, especially divine punishment or destruction.
An active participle of أَخَذَ; the Quranic contexts use it for taking or grasping an object or person.

senses.definition: One who adopts, chooses, or takes someone or something as an associate, object, or specified role.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of اتَّخَذَ; it may describe taking someone as a companion, lover, supporter, or other chosen associate, or taking something for a designated purpose.

senses.definition: Adopting, choosing, acquiring, or making something or someone into a specified role.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of اتَّخَذَ, covering deliberate adoption or constitution, including taking something as an object of allegiance or worship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid or assist someone, literally by taking the person's hand or arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, figurative use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prevent, restrain, or withhold someone from doing what he intends.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom portraying restraint as laying hold of the person's hand or arm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To derive or deduce a word, phrase, or meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed figurative use describing derivation from a source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For travel or exertion to weaken or exhaust someone by taking away strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object understood with the verb is the person's strength or vigor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clip or cut off hair or the moustache.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with hair or moustache as the material removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a violent assault on someone and wound him severely; also, to assail him with the tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes physical assault and the idiomatic use for vehement verbal attack or vituperation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a road, course, manner, or prudent line of action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a road, direction, precaution, or adopted course of conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin, commence, or set about doing something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verb of inception, commonly followed by an activity or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eye to see, notice, or regard someone as worthy of attention.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression concerning visual notice or esteem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To captivate or fascinate someone by enchantment or charm, especially to restrain him from sexual relations with others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II lexical use associated with magical fascination and sexual restraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make milk sour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II use with milk as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For combatants to take hold of one another in fighting or wrestling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes reciprocal seizing in combat, including wrestling to throw an opponent down.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, manufacture, or prepare a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII use with an object such as a bow, waterskin, dish, or medicine; this is broader Classical usage than the Quranic appointing construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way or manner of life, including the manners, disposition, fashion, or conduct one adopts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in expressions for people who follow another group's way of life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mansions of the Moon; by another explanation, stars cast at devils listening furtively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lunar-mansion explanation is identified as the more correct one in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of taking or taking with the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive derived from أَخَذَ and used as a variant nominal form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark made with a hot iron on a camel's side when disease is feared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical livestock term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Heaviness of the stomach and indigestion in a young camel caused by milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized ailment term for a young camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal affected by something resembling madness or demoniacal possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a camel, young camel, sheep, or goat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person affected by inflammation, pain, swelling, or ophthalmia of the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The corresponding noun أُخُذٌ denotes the eye ailment itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Inflammation, pain, and swelling of the eye; ophthalmia.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the eye ailment, distinct from the adjectival use أَخِذٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Places of abode or settled locations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for people taking their places of residence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manner or technique of taking hold of an opponent in wrestling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for a wrestler's hold; its plural is أُخَذٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enchantment or fascination that captivates or restrains someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to a charm, bead, or incantation believed to captivate or restrain, including restraining a husband from other women.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pitfall dug for catching a lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized hunting term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The period shortly after sunset regarded as an unfavorable time for striking fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in an idiomatic expression about hastening to produce fire before that time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pool, basin, or water receptacle formed by a torrent or dug to retain water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a natural pool left by floodwater, a place where animals gather to drink, or a constructed watering-trough; variant forms include إِخَاذَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who or something that has been taken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial use of the root, separate from the specialized noun for a captive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A captive or prisoner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine is formed with ة; the term can occur in sayings about a captive taken by an army.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strange or foreign old man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land taken or allocated for oneself, especially waste land brought into cultivation or granted for cultivation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe land claimed by a person or granted by a ruler or imam when it is not already another's property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The handle of a shield of the type called حَجَفَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical object term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing taken by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive noun describing an object seized forcibly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who takes eagerly or greedily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used pejoratively of someone who eagerly takes things and then quickly throws them away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel beginning to become fat or to grow old.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival use with the plural أَوَاخِذُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk that bites or stings the tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive term synonymous with قَارِصٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place from which or at which something is taken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a source or capture point, such as places from which birds are taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The source or basis from which a word, phrase, or meaning is derived.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A terminological use concerning derivation or interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way or route that one takes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a chosen route, including taking the nearest way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man withheld from women by enchantment or charm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive description of the enchantment construction associated with أَخَّذَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long hair requiring to be clipped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival use applied to hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who lowers or stoops the head because of eye inflammation, pain, disease, or submission.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lowered posture may result from ophthalmia or pain, and can also be described as lowly or submissive because of illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For milk to become sour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I lexical use describing souring of milk.

cautions: The historical Quran citations embedded in Lane are retained as lexical evidence but are not treated as modern verse locations unless independently confirmed by QAC.
The active participle آخذ is presented under its normalized singular citation form; Quranic contextual renderings vary between taking and grasping.
